headline: Proving AI Works
thesis: As EdTech Week and the StartEd CEO Summit convene in New York, the sector's hardest question is whether AI is delivering measurable learning value.
summary: Evidence is the story. A University of Maryland randomized trial found only about 15% of students chose to use its AI study assistant and the provost said there are no clear findings, echoing EDUCAUSE's #1 2027 priority of finding where AI adds real value and Instructure data showing AI tools missing the top 100 Canvas integrations. In K-12, EdSurge and EdTech Digest push back on blanket AI bans, Google ties Classroom into Gemini, and Brookings urges caution. Events ahead: EdTech Week NYC (this week), 1EdTech's Technical Congress (Oct 19–21) and ISTE+ASCD Boston (Oct 27–30).
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · October 13, 2026 · Direct site fetches were unavailable, so items come from search-indexed results; search-metadata dates can be inconsistent and EdTech Week dates vary by listing (Oct 12–16 vs. Oct 13–15 vs. Oct 14–15). Most sources had no new dated news today.
